gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: Applications ___ be submitted in person, not by post.
It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have rushed the final checks — now there are errors everywhere.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes a past action with bad results: shouldn't have rushed.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: ___ you swim when you were four years old?
gaps.explanation: 'Could' asks about past ability: Could you swim.

gaps.sentence: I didn't ___ to like coffee, but now I drink it every day.
gaps.hint: negative of used to, spelled use
gaps.explanation: In the negative, 'used to' becomes 'didn't use to': use.
